# Error Handling and Exceptional Conditions (ERR)

Errors must fail safely: deny access, keep data consistent and reveal nothing useful to an attacker. This covers OWASP Top 10:2025 A10, a new category.

## SCS-ERR-01 Show generic errors to users; keep details in server logs

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Error responses and error screens MUST be generic and MUST NOT expose stack traces, exception messages, internal paths, SQL, server names, versions or debug information. Full error details MUST be logged on the server only, linked by a correlation ID.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Register AddProblemDetails() and AddExceptionHandler<GlobalExceptionHandler>(); call app.UseExceptionHandler() outside Development.
- Return ProblemDetails with a generic title and a traceId. Never return ex.Message, ex.ToString() or inner exception text.
- The developer exception page runs whenever ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT is Development; make sure production servers never run as Development.
- .NET 10: exceptions handled by IExceptionHandler are no longer logged by default; log them in the handler.
- Do not set EnableDetailedErrors or EnableSensitiveDataLogging outside Development.

Verification: Force an exception in staging and confirm the response contains only a generic message and trace ID.

## SCS-ERR-02 Fail closed and leave no half-finished work

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: When a security check, dependency or operation fails, the code MUST deny the action rather than allow it. Multi-step operations MUST either complete fully or roll back, so that a failure leaves data in a known state.

Implementation (all stacks):

- An exception inside an authorization, validation or token check results in denial (401/403/400), never in success.
- Never swallow exceptions with an empty catch. Catch specific exceptions and handle them deliberately.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Wrap multi-step changes in a transaction (EF Core SaveChanges or BeginTransaction), or use explicit states (Pending, Processing, Done, Failed) for long-running work and SAP postings.
- Use idempotency keys for operations that may be retried (payments, SAP postings, approvals).
- Use optimistic concurrency (rowversion) or unique constraints to stop double-submit races.

Verification: Fault-injection tests (for example SAP or database unavailable mid-operation) confirm access is denied and data stays consistent.
